subject: Deployment mode preference validation — Dedicated vs Private VPC (data isolation)
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Shah <pshah@fintrust.com>; Tom Walker <tom.walker@fintrust.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 11 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Deployment mode preference validation — Dedicated vs Private VPC (data isolation)

Hi Priya / Tom,

Great to speak earlier — thanks for walking through FinTrust's high-level use case and the sensitivity around PII-derived scoring metadata. As promised, a concise recap and a couple of clarifying questions so we can recommend the right deployment mode (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC/on-prem).

Recap from our call:
- Workloads: real-time credit scoring (sub-100ms SLO for short prompts) + nightly batch embeddings for analytics.
- Data sensitivity: customer PII flows in request payloads; security team requires strict separation of customer data and cryptographic controls.
- Compliance drivers: SOC 2 + impending regional data processing agreement.

Questions to confirm your isolation expectations (these will determine whether Dedicated or Private VPC is recommended):
1) Physical isolation: Is co-tenancy on dedicated hardware acceptable if networking and disk access are segregated via tenant assignment, or do you require a customer-controlled VPC (customer-managed network + private peering)?
2) Key management: Do you need Redwood to integrate with your KMS/HSM (bring-your-own-key) or can keys be managed by Redwood?
3) Audit requirements: Do you need streaming audit logs with retention under your control and separate from Redwood's multi-tenant logs?
4) On-prem necessity: Is air-gapped on-prem deployment a hard requirement, or is VPC with strict egress controls acceptable?

Next steps I propose:
- You: quick confirmation on Q1–Q4 above (one short email will suffice).
- Us: I'll loop in Dev (cc'd) to run a high-level ops feasibility check and produce a tailored recommendation + one-pager comparing Dedicated vs Private VPC by Monday.
- Optional: if helpful, we can schedule a short call with your security architect and our Infrastructure lead to walk the technical checklist.

I've attached a one-pager that outlines the differences in deployment modes; also added the security questionnaire we started filling in during the call.

Thanks —
Aditya Rao
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0199

Attachments: redwood_dedicated_vs_vpc_onepager.pdf (pdf), fintrust_data_handling_questions.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Priya Shah <pshah@fintrust.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 11 Apr 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Deployment mode preference validation — Dedicated vs Private VPC (data isolation)

Thanks Aditya — quick answers below to help you narrow recommendation: 

1) Physical isolation: Co-tenancy on dedicated hardware is acceptable only if cryptographic separation is provable (separate tenant IDs, no shared disk volumes, and per-tenant memory scrub on eviction). Our legal team is wary of any shared control plane for sensitive workloads.
2) Key management: We require BYOK (customer-managed keys in our Azure Key Vault).
3) Audit requirements: We need audit logs that can be exported to our SIEM with retention controlled by our policies (min 7 years for some event types).
4) On-prem: Not necessary at this point; VPC with private peering and no public egress is fine.

One more: do you have examples of customers running private VPC with BYOK and exportable audit streams? If so, please point me to references or anonymized case studies.

—Priya
Security & Privacy Lead, FinTrust
pshah@fintrust.com | +1 (212) 555-0147

Dev — quick tech ask (can you confirm by EOD):
- Can Redwood Private (VPC) support BYOK where keys live in the customer's Azure Key Vault and Redwood performs encryption operations via a customer-managed endpoint?
- For Dedicated (reserved capacity) model, can we provide per-tenant cryptographic isolation guarantees (separate tenant IDs, ephemeral memory scrub, and verified no-shared-disk)? If any control-plane elements remain multi-tenant, please call that out.
- Audit logs: can we stream raw audit events to a customer SIEM endpoint (TLS push or S3 transfer with customer-controlled retention)?

I sketched a short internal check matrix as a reference (attached). If we have references for customers with similar needs (anonymized), please include them in your reply.

Aditya

Aditya / Priya — quick technical thumbs-up and notes below. High-level: Private VPC is the safest path to meet FinTrust's stated controls; Dedicated can work but requires stricter contractual guarantees and ops checks. Details: 

1) BYOK: Supported for Private VPC. We can integrate with your Azure Key Vault via a customer-managed endpoint; Redwood will never persist raw keys. We'll provide integration docs and a short runbook for key rotation.

2) Per-tenant cryptographic isolation for Dedicated: We can provide tenant-scoped encryption keys and separate tenant IDs. However, Dedicated’s control plane (orchestration layer) remains Redwood-managed in current product design. We can negotiate stronger SLAs and audit commitments in enterprise contracts, but if legal requires control-plane isolation, Private VPC is required.

3) Memory/disk isolation: For Dedicated we guarantee no shared block volumes and provide disk encryption at rest per instance, plus a process for memory scrub on container/process teardown. We will include our memory-scrub proof steps in the technical appendix.

4) Audit streaming: We support push-based audit exports to customer SIEM (TLS endpoint) and S3 transfer with IAM role for customer retention control. We can scope events (request metadata, model version IDs, auth events) per your compliance needs.

5) References: We have two anonymized case studies (financial services) that used Private VPC + BYOK with audit streaming; I'll add these to the one-pager and share links.

Next steps (proposed):
- I’ll produce a 1-page technical appendix showing exactly which components run in the customer's VPC vs Redwood-managed control plane, and a sample key-integration diagram.
- Aditya: suggest we hold a 30-min technical call with Priya and your infra/security team mid-next-week.

Regards,
Dev Patel
Infra Lead, Redwood Inference
dev_patel@redwood.ai
